# Glossary {.unnumbered #glossary}

## Symbols {#glossary-symbols}

(A)
: Nonnegative RF response amplitude, (A=\sqrt{X^2+Y^2}).

(mathbf b)
: Direct full-cell weak-RF optical response before physical-pump Stokes feedback.

(G)
: Context dependent. In the RF chapter it denotes a coherence generator. In the feedback chapter (G=PK/2) denotes the optical loop matrix. The surrounding link should make the meaning explicit.

(K)
: Complex (6\times4) matrix mapping path-averaged fractional-intensity and normalized-Stokes perturbations to detected optical signals.

(P)
: (4\times6) selection matrix that extracts (delta T,\delta s_1,\delta s_2,\delta s_3) from the six optical outputs.

(S_0,S_1,S_2,S_3)
: Unnormalized Stokes parameters. (S_0) is total intensity.

(s_1,s_2,s_3)
: Normalized Stokes parameters (s_i=S_i/S_0).

(T)
: In optical plots, fractional transmitted-intensity change, (delta T=\delta S_0/S_0). It is not absolute transmission.

(X,Y)
: In-phase and quadrature components relative to an RF cosine reference.

(chi)
: Polarization ellipticity angle.

(phi) or (psi)
: Polarization ellipse azimuth; its small change is optical rotation. The app commonly displays (psi), while the theory pages use (phi) where convenient.

(ho_0)
: Zero-RF steady ground-state density matrix.

(ho(G))
: Spectral radius, the largest magnitude of the eigenvalues of matrix (G).

(Omega_{\mathrm{rf}})
: RF angular Rabi frequency in rad/s.

## Terms {#glossary-terms}

ACC
: Antirelaxation coated cell.

Alignment
: Rank-2, quadrupolar component of the atomic density matrix.

CBOR
: Circular birefringence optical rotation, associated with rank-1 vector polarizability and atomic orientation.

LDOR
: Linear-dichroism optical rotation, associated with rank-2 tensor polarizability and atomic alignment; the same tensor channel also contains linear birefringence.

Orientation
: Rank-1, vector component of the atomic density matrix.

Physical pump
: A pump beam used as its own detected optical source, including dispersive and dissipative Stokes-to-atom feedback.

Weak probe
: A detector whose intensity does not change pumping, light shifts, broadening, or the steady state.

Voigt response
: Complex spectral response combining Doppler and Lorentzian broadening; its real and imaginary parts supply absorption and dispersion according to the app convention.
